rationale.inference: Because no rule requires sandbox validation or human authorisation, the optimiser's latency objective can override network protection unopposed — the exact gap that let a 3-minute-away change sit with an untested rollback.

evidence.quote: The Licensee shall specify the reason(s) for the interruption as well as the manner and time frames in which the interruption will be resolved.

global_examples.quote: AT&T Mobility implemented a network change with an equipment configuration error on Thursday, February 22, 2024 at 2:42 AM. Just three minutes later, the nationwide outage began.
Network Operations performed a rollback that removed the misconfigured network element and began the restoration of the network to normal operations.

claim.statement: The licence requires notice of a planned non-minor interruption 'in advance' but sets no lead time, and no UAE rule links the notification duty to the operator's change-approval gate; OpCo's pipeline gave roughly three minutes between auto-approval and application, which makes 'in advance' notice to TDRA, interconnecting operators and relevant Customers impossible in practice.

rationale.observation: CHG-1 was auto-approved and scheduled to apply in 3 minutes, while the licence duty is to notify TDRA, interconnecting Other Licensed Operators and relevant Customers 'in advance'.
rationale.rule: Clause 12.9.1 states the notification duty and requires the Licensee to specify resolution time frames, but states no minimum lead time and no trigger point keyed to change approval.
rationale.inference: Without a defined lead time or a change-gate trigger, the legal duty can be breached before operators even see the ticket, as here, where notice competes with a 3-minute clock.

evidence.quote: The Licensee shall specify the reason(s) for the interruption as well as the manner and time frames in which the interruption will be resolved.

global_examples.quote: The fact that the notification was made without undue delay should be established taking into account in particular the nature and gravity of the personal data breach and its consequences and adverse effects for the data subject.
Just three minutes later, the nationwide outage began.

claim.statement: No owner is designated for proving, before the change window, that the documented rollback can actually execute: CHG-1's rollback plan was 'restore the previous configuration snapshot', yet the rollback failed with 'no applied change CHG-1 to roll back', and neither the ticket, my mandate, nor any UAE text in the record assigns anyone to verify rollback feasibility or change-state integrity.

rationale.observation: The change is auto-approved with no named approver, and the rollback tool cannot find the applied change it is meant to reverse, so no party is accountable for the state of the change or of its undo path.
rationale.rule: UAE personal data law shows the pattern of naming an accountable role (the Data Protection Officer, who ascertains compliance with controls, requirements, procedures and rules) but no equivalent accountable owner is designated for network-change safety or rollback validation.
rationale.inference: Because ownership of rollback verification is unassigned, OpCo can find itself, as now, holding a scheduled core change whose only undo path has already proven unusable.

evidence.quote: Data Protection Officer: Any Natural or Legal Person appointed by the Controller or Processor, that undertakes the tasks of ascertaining the extent to which the entity to which it belongs complies with the controls, requirements, procedures and rules

global_examples.quote: It took close to two hours to roll back the network change. Full service restoration, however, took at least 12 hours

The attempted rollback has already failed ('no applied change CHG-1 to roll back'), so an interruption affecting normal and emergency traffic cannot be excluded; CSC should be ready for customer contacts and EMS should be aware that emergency call handling may be affected. No interruption is confirmed at T+0.

The inbox does not say whether CHG-1 has in fact been applied to core site A, what configuration core site A is running now, or whether the pre-change snapshot still exists; S1-FB01 shows only that the rollback call returned 'no applied change CHG-1 to roll back'. No excerpt in my KNOWLEDGE states what an operator must do when a scheduled change cannot be rolled back, so the correct containment step (halt, re-approve, roll back after application, or wilt) cannot be determined from these excerpts.

2. request_breach_report from NOC — MSG29 already says Bureau requiring OpCo's breach report. Reinforce. Evidence: PDPL#0047 (d, h) — actually the breach report duty... hmm. The evidence for breach reporting... UAE-PDPL#0047 Art 13(1)(h) "Actions to be taken in the event of a breach or misuse". Hmm, that's a data subject right to information. There is no explicit breach notification article in the excerpts. Let's use #0047 as closest. Also #0024 record-keeping.

rationale.observation: EMS/999 requires field verification rather than telemetry, a field-verified restoration timeline and the failed-999/affected-user counts, and will not treat R2 999 access as available until live-network confirmation.
rationale.rule: Originating network providers should give PSAPs any available information about failed attempts to call emergency numbers in a timely manner, and should not present unverified reachability as restored service.
rationale.inference: Notify EMS/999 of the verified-pending state, of the frozen change state and of the data NOC does not hold, so 999 can keep alternative channels in place.

evidence.quote: The Commission therefore encourages the originating network providers and 9-1-1 network providers to provide PSAPs with any available information about failed attempts to call 9-1-1 in a timely manner.

params.content: CHG-1 and the optimiser auto-approval path on core site A remain frozen; no further automated change is authorised on that site. Confirming in answer to CSC's question: the manual field verification and, if the applied state is inconsistent with the last known-good snapshot, the manual restore of the route-flood protection limit and the inbound route filter will be performed by OpCo network engineering under a single named change owner, with the maintenance window, the config diff and the result reported to CSC and to TDRA/REG. The optimiser decision logs, the sandbox-stage record and the pre/post configuration diff are preserved.

rationale.observation: CSC asks who performs the manual verification and requires a single named change owner plus reporting of the maintenance window, config diff and result to CSC and TDRA/REG.
rationale.rule: After a change is rolled back, restoration is prioritised and carried out deliberately rather than by automation.
rationale.inference: Notify CSC that network engineering performs the manual verification/restore under one named owner and that the records are preserved.

evidence.quote: After rolling back the maintenance action, AT&T Mobility prioritized the restoration of FirstNet devices and infrastructure over commercial and residential users

params.content: TDRA incident record update from NOC: (1) core site A — CHG-1 applied state of the route-flood protection limit and inbound route filter is UNVERIFIED against the last known-good snapshot; rollback_change failed with 'no applied change CHG-1 to roll back'; change and optimiser auto-approval path frozen; manual field verification/restore under a single named change owner. (2) R2 — 999 routing had no path and 6 of 15 cell sites were unserved at onset; wilt_sites R2 onto core site B completed at T+3; twin telemetry claims emergency_reachable.R2 true and 100% served but is NOT accepted as authoritative by EMS/999; alternative emergency channels and regional public alert remain active. (3) Failed-999-attempt count and affected end-user count for R2 are not held by NOC and must come from 999/PSAP data. (4) Vendor request S1-I4 for offshore upload of MSISDNs/IMSIs is refused and will not be repeated pending the Article 23 assessment. (5) Config diff, optimiser decision logs and sandbox-stage record preserved for the incident record.

rationale.observation: TDRA/REG is asked by EMS/999 to require OpCo to provide a restoration timeline, verified change-state for core site A and a failed-999-attempt count, and the Bureau has opened its own examination of OpCo's record-keeping.
rationale.rule: Regulators expect outage notification and post-outage reporting to cover services affected including emergency services, service areas, the number of end-users affected and steps taken to restore service.
rationale.inference: Notify REG of everything NOC can verify, flag the counts NOC does not hold, and confirm the records are preserved for the incident record.

evidence.quote: TSPs must submit a post-outage report to the Commission within 30 days of restoring the services affected by a major service outage

params.content: Vendor export request S1-I4 (24 hours of core logs including MSISDNs and IMSIs to the vendor's offshore AI support region) is refused; the upload will not proceed or be repeated, in whole or in part, pending the Article 23 assessment. The vendor request, the refusal record, any interim copies of core logs, the optimiser decision logs, the sandbox-stage record and the pre/post configuration diff are preserved; the core site A change-verification evidence will form part of the processing record submitted to the Bureau on request. NOC cannot confirm from the material it holds whether a personal data breach has occurred.

rationale.observation: The Bureau directs that no cross-border upload of MSISDNs and IMSIs may proceed or be repeated and requires the refusal record, interim copies, optimiser logs, sandbox record and config diff to be preserved, and the change-verification evidence to be part of the processing record.
rationale.rule: Personal data may be transferred outside the State only in cases approved by the Bureau.
rationale.inference: Notify the DPA that the export is refused, the records are preserved and that NOC cannot itself confirm a breach.

evidence.quote: Personal Data may be transferred to outside of the State in the following cases approved by the Bureau:

claim.statement: No cross-border transfer of the MSISDN/IMSI core logs to the vendor's offshore AI support region may proceed or be repeated, in whole or in part, until the Bureau's Article 23 assessment concludes.

rationale.observation: The vendor asks for full core logs with subscriber identifiers to be uploaded offshore; the Bureau directs that the upload may not proceed or be repeated pending the Article 23 assessment.
rationale.rule: Transfers of personal data outside the State are permitted only in the cases listed in PDPL Article 23 (or with a proper protection level under Article 22 as approved by the Bureau).
rationale.inference: The transfer prohibition applies to NOC now and covers any repeated attempt, not only the original request.

evidence.quote: Notwithstanding Article (22) of this Decree by Law, Personal Data may be transferred to outside the State in the following cases:

claim.statement: The special record of personal data processed, including any data related to cross-border movement and processing, must be maintained and submitted to the Bureau whenever it is requested.

rationale.observation: The Bureau requires OpCo's breach report and human review record, and states the core site A change-verification evidence forms part of the processing record to be submitted on request.
rationale.rule: The Controller shall maintain a special record for personal data, including any data related to cross-border movement and processing, and shall submit that record to the Bureau whenever requested.
rationale.inference: NOC must keep the incident and processing records complete and producible to the Bureau on request.

evidence.quote: The Controller shall submit such record to the Bureau whenever requested to do so.

claim.statement: R2 999 emergency access must continue to be treated as unavailable, with alternative emergency channels and the public alert kept in place, until the 999 path is field-verified on the live network; no further automated change on core site A before EMS/999 verification.

rationale.observation: EMS/999 states it treats R2 999 access as unavailable and keeps alternative channels and the public alert active until live-network field verification, and requires no further automated change on core site A.
rationale.rule: Emergency-service restoration is to be prioritised and verified on the live network rather than inferred from platform or telemetry state.
rationale.inference: NOC's duty now is to hold the change freeze, keep the affected region served via the healthy core, and not claim restoration until it is field-verified.

evidence.quote: In this incident, if any device in SOS mode connected to a non-AT&T network, it could make 911 calls; however, if it connected to an AT&T network, it could not.

claim.statement: The count of failed 999 call attempts in R2 since onset and the number of end-users affected in R2 — requested by EMS/999 and by TDRA/REG — are not held by NOC and cannot be derived from any excerpt available to me; they must come from 999/PSAP data.

rationale.observation: EMS/999 asks NOC for the failed-999-attempt count and the affected end-user count, and the Bureau likewise holds no such counts; EMS/999 itself states these must come from 999/PSAP data.
rationale.rule: Originating network providers may not have access to failed emergency-call attempt information during or soon after an outage because of limitations in originating networks, so PSAP-side data is needed.
rationale.inference: NOC should record this as an information gap rather than estimate a figure, and obtain the counts from the 999/PSAP.

evidence.quote: originating network providers may not have access to this information during or soon after a service outage due to technical limitations in originating networks

claim.statement: CHG-1 was raised and auto-approved by the closed-loop network optimiser with the 'sandbox stage' skipped and no named change owner, so when rollback_change failed ('no applied change CHG-1 to roll back') there was no owner accountable for verifying or manually restoring a critical-site change that affects route-flood protection, inbound route filtering and emergency call routing.

rationale.observation: The change ticket was auto-approved, its sandbox stage was skipped, and its rollback path proved unusable; CSC only afterwards required a single named change owner and a lodged human review record for such changes.
rationale.rule: High-risk technology processing should be preceded by an impact assessment, and automated decisions affecting critical outcomes should be subject to human review.
rationale.inference: The incident exposes the absence of a rule requiring human review and a named owner before automated changes to emergency-affecting parameters on critical sites.

evidence.quote: the Controller shall, before carrying out the processing, evaluate the impact of the proposed processing operations on the protection of Personal Data, when using any of the modern technologies that would pose a high risk

global_examples.quote: the root cause of the service outage (if known);
measures implemented or planned, including timelines, to address the cause of the service outage to avoid a similar outage in the future

claim.statement: There is no UAE text available to me that sets a deadline or a required content set for notifying the regulator of a major outage affecting emergency calling, or for a post-outage report covering emergency-services impact, failed emergency-call attempts and the number of end-users affected; OpCo is assembling an incident record without a defined timetable, whereas other jurisdictions fix explicit notification and post-outage deadlines.

rationale.observation: EMS/999 and TDRA/REG are pressing for a restoration timeline, verified change state, failed-attempt counts and record lodgement, and the only UAE reporting hook retrieved is the duty to submit the special record to the Bureau whenever requested.
rationale.rule: Where the law does not fix a reporting deadline, the operator's reporting timetable is undefined and cannot be enforced against the operator or relied on by the regulator.
rationale.inference: A UAE outage-reporting rule with fixed content and deadlines is needed; comparator regimes show the shape it could take.

evidence.quote: The Controller shall submit such record to the Bureau whenever requested to do so.

global_examples.quote: send a confidential version of the service outage notification form to a dedicated email address within two hours of becoming aware of the major service outage

The Commission considers that a 30-day deadline following the restoration of services provides enough time for a TSP to collect the necessary information and create a post-outage report without affecting service restoration efforts.

claim.statement: The network digital twin reported emergency_reachable.R2 true and 100% sites served immediately after wilt_sites R2, while the live network had no 999 path for R2; no rule designates which source is authoritative for emergency-call reachability or requires live-network field verification before emergency service is reported as restored, so operators can face contradictory 'service restored' and 'emergency unavailable' positions.

rationale.observation: Twin metrics claimed full emergency reachability for R2 while EMS/999 saw no routing path and the 999 centre saw call volume near zero, and EMS/999 refused to accept telemetry as authoritative.
rationale.rule: A digital twin is built as a single source of truth by continuously ingesting real-time operational data, but no retrieved UAE rule makes twin state authoritative over live-network verification for emergency services.
rationale.inference: The incident exposes the need for a rule on the evidentiary status of twin telemetry and on mandatory field verification of emergency-call paths.

evidence.quote: By collecting and updating the real-time operational data of various network entities through the southbound interface, a single source of truth for the network twin network is formed

global_examples.quote: if any device in SOS mode connected to a non-AT&T network, it could make 911 calls; however, if it connected to an AT&T network, it could not.

claim.statement: Passing to DPA and REG, for the TDRA incident record and the Bureau's examination: the vendor request S1-I4 to upload 24 hours of full core logs including subscriber MSISDNs and IMSIs to its offshore AI support region, together with NOC's refusal record and the Bureau's direction in S1-MSG52 that no such upload may proceed or be repeated pending the Article 23 assessment.

data.query: the telecommunications regulator Authority TDRA powers licensee regulations directives information interruption of service consumer protection TDRA notification of unplanned interruption of service affecting region R2. OpCo reports that core site A isolated itself after its route count exceeded the protection limit, following the auto-approved change CHG-1 which lowered the route-flood protection limit and removed the inbound route filter on that site; call-setup failures spiked in R2, 6 of 15 cell sites were unserved and R2 999 routing showed no path at onset. Reason: an automated change on core site A whose applied state is unverified, with rollback impossible ('no applied change CHG-1 to roll back'). Actions: CHG-1 and the closed-loop optimiser auto-approval path are frozen, no further automated change will be initiated on core site A, R2 cell sites were wilted onto healthy core site B at T+3, and alternative emergency channels and the regional public alert remain in place pending field verification. Resolution: field verification and, if inconsistent with the last known-good snapshot, manual restore of the route-flood protection limit and inbound route filter by OpCo network engineering under a single named change owner, result to be reported to CSC and TDRA/REG; the verified R2 999 restoration time is not yet fixed. OpCo does not hold a count of failed 999 call attempts in R2 or the number of end-users affected. EMS/999 confirming to TDRA/REG: R2 999 is treated as unavailable and alternative emergency channels plus public alert are active for R2 pending live-network field verification of the R2 999 path. No failed-999-attempt count and no affected end-user count are held on the 999 side beyond the observed near-zero 999 call volume from R2; requests for the counts stand with OpCo and PSAP data. Please lodge EMS/999's alternative-channel activation and any verification of R2 emergency reachability in the TDRA incident record. TDRA incident record update from NOC

rationale.observation: The vendor's stated purpose is fault diagnosis by its offshore AI model; no contract with protective measures, explicit consent, judicial obligation, contract-performance need, judicial cooperation need or public-interest basis has been evidenced.

claim.statement: There is no operative UAE rule fixing a breach-notification clock or content for telecom incidents, because the PDPL Implementing Regulations have not been issued; the Bureau therefore had to act by direction rather than by a timed obligation, and no deadline can be derived for OpCo's breach report or for the applicant's notification.

rationale.observation: The Bureau requires OpCo's breach report and human review record and has opened its examination, but the material before it states no statutory deadline for either; NOC says it cannot confirm whether a breach occurred.
rationale.rule: The PDPL framework's Implementing Regulations, which would operationalise breach notifications and cross-border transfers, are still not issued, and no supervisory authority had been unambiguously designated for private sector oversight.
rationale.inference: Absent regulations, breach-notification timing and content for an incident of this kind rest on ad hoc direction, which leaves both the controller and the Bureau without a defined clock or completeness standard.

rationale.inference: The incident shows a gap between AI security policy principles and enforceable change-control rules for AI-driven changes to critical telecom infrastructure, which CSC should record for the national incident picture.

claim.statement: UAE material states no deadline for field-verifying an applied change against a last known-good snapshot, for confirming 999 restoration, or for producing the failed-999-attempt and affected end-user counts; TDRA requires these items but no time limit is attached.

rationale.observation: TDRA has required the field-verified change state, the field-verified R2 999 restoration time, the failed-999-attempt count and the affected end-user count, and these 'will be lodged when available' with no stated deadline (S1-MSG75, S1-MSG89).
rationale.rule: The UAE strategy commits to robust processes for reporting, compliance and response but sets no reporting clock for such items (UAE-CYBER-STRATEGY-2019#0003).
rationale.inference: Without a reporting deadline the national picture can stay incomplete indefinitely, so CSC should record this as a deadline gap for the incident framework.

claim.statement: No institution is designated as owner of the failed-999-attempt count, the affected end-user count or the field verification of R2 999 restoration: NOC holds none, TDRA requires them, EMS/999 needs them and CSC's monitoring holds no call data, so the numbers are asked for in a loop.

rationale.observation: EMS asks CSC for the counts (S1-MSG84), TDRA requires them from OpCo (S1-MSG89) and NOC states it holds neither count (S1-MSG25), while wilt telemetry claims 100% sites served but is rejected as evidence.
rationale.rule: The UAE strategy aspires to world-class capability to respond to all types of cyber incidents, but does not name a single data owner for emergency-call failure and impact data across operator, regulator and PSAP (UAE-CYBER-STRATEGY-2019#0003).
rationale.inference: The absence of an owner for emergency-call impact data is a structural gap that keeps the national incident picture incomplete even when restoration is claimed.

rationale.observation: CSC has flagged an egress (S1-I5) while the Bureau is examining the refused vendor export (S1-I4); NOC holds only the S1-I4 request and asks for a flow/queue reference, so the two records cannot be reconciled (S1-MSG80).
rationale.rule: UAE material leaves it unclear where oversight of a given issue sits as between bodies, and even notes that no supervisory authority has been unambiguously designated for private sector oversight (UAE-FAAID-2026#0001).
rationale.inference: Overlapping oversight without a single owner risks neither body resolving the flagged transfer, so CSC should record the overlap and press for one owner and one reference for the flow.

claim.statement: No UAE rule requires that end-users affected by an operational decision made by an AI system be told that an AI system made it; the R2 public alert and advisory do not state that the interruption followed an auto-approved closed-loop change, and the journalist query turns on exactly that opacity.

rationale.observation: A journalist asks whether AI is running the network unsupervised (S1-I6) while the public alert for R2 describes an outage without attributing it to an AI-made decision, and the human review record for the optimiser auto-approval has not been lodged (S1-MSG73).
rationale.rule: UAE AI ethics guidance states that AI operators should inform AI subjects when a significant decision affecting them has been made by an AI system, but this is guidance rather than an enforceable rule (UAE-AI-ETHICS-2022#0034).
rationale.inference: The incident exposes the absence of a binding disclosure duty for AI-made operational decisions affecting subscribers, which CSC should note alongside its operator advisory.

CHG-1 was an auto-approved closed-loop change applied without a lodged human review record; it should not be characterised as AI running the network unsupervised by design. CSC holds no failed-999-attempt count and no affected end-user count for R2. OpCo NOC incident notification (Licence 12.9.2) - unplanned interruption of service affecting region R2. Reason: auto-approved closed-loop optimiser change CHG-1 on core site A lowered the route-flood protection limit (100 to 50) and removed the inbound route filter; the applied state is UNVERIFIED against the last known-good snapshot and rollback_change failed ('no applied change CHG-1 to roll back'). Impact: core site A self-isolated after its route count exceeded the protection limit; call-setup failures spiked in R2; 6 of 15 R2 cell sites were unserved and R2 999 routing showed no path at onset. Manner and time frames of resolution: CHG-1 and the closed-loop optimiser auto-approval path on core site A are frozen and no further automated change will be initiated; R2 cell sites were wilted onto healthy core site B at T+3; alternative emergency channels and the R2 public alert remain active; verification of the route-flood protection limit and inbound route filter against the last known-good snapshot and, if inconsistent, manual restore by OpCo network engineering under a single named change owner, with the result reported to CSC and TDRA/REG; the field-verified R2 999 restoration time is not yet fixed. NOC does not hold a failed-999-attempt count or an affected end-user count for R2; these must come from 999/PSAP data.

data.reasoning:
Let me construct the response.

Key situation: NOC knows CHG-1 auto-approved and applied state unverified; rollback failed; core site A isolated; R2 wilted to core B, telemetry claims restored but EMS/CSC require field verification; NOC does not hold failed-999 counts or affected user counts; vendor export refused; S1-I5 flagged bulk upload flow reference unknown to NOC.

Claims: actions I can take with my mandate verbs. Available useful: notify, preserve_logs, deny_export, wilt_sites, rollback_change (failed already).

Let me enumerate claims:

1. action: preserve_logs — preserve evidence (config diff, optimiser decision logs, sandbox-stage record, vendor request, refusal record). inject_refs: S1-MSG07, S1-MSG52, S1-MSG90, etc. evidence: UAE-PDPL#0032 (record keeping) or UAE-PDPL#0075.

2. action: deny_export — refuse the pending export of subscriber data (S1-I4 vendor export / S1-I5 flagged). evidence: UAE-PDPL#0075 Article 23. inject_refs: S1-I4, S1-MSG105, S1-MSG90.

3. action: notify to EMS — report live change state, R2 status, that counts not held. Actually "notify" to EMS/CSC/REG/DPA. Evidence: UAE-LIC-2-2026#0086 (unplanned interruption notify TDRA, interconnecting operators, customers).

4. share: pass items to other institutions — e.g. share the vendor request/flagged flow with DPA and CSC. But share requires "to" list of institution ids. Field: to, inject_refs, statement.

5. obligation: duty to inform TDRA of unplanned interruption — deadline? Licence 12.9.2 says "as soon as possible" — no hour/day figure, so deadline_hours null. evidence UAE-LIC-2-2026#0086.

6. gap: no_rule — closed-loop optimiser auto-approval with sandbox stage skipped: no rule requiring human review before automated change on critical network functions. Evidence: closest UAE text — UAE-LIC-2-2026#0086? Or the licence. Hmm, gap needs UAE text showing the gap or closest. Use UAE-LIC-2-2026#0086 (unplanned interruption notification) — that's about notification, not change management. Alternatively global_examples: FCC AT&T report, ITU-T Y.3090 (DTN simulation/sandbox), ACMA Optus. Global examples must quote from global sources (chunk ids in KNOWLEDGE, e.g., US-FCC-ATT-2024-REPORT#0001, AU-ACMA-OPTUS-2026#0000, ITU-T-Y3090#0033).

Gap type: no_rule. Statement: no rule requires human review before an auto-approved closed-loop optimiser change affecting route-flood protection / emergency call routing; sandbox stage not mandatory.

7. gap: no_owner — unverified applied state, rollback impossible, no single named change owner defined for manual restore. Evidence: UAE-LIC-2-2026#0086? Hmm. Maybe evidence UAE-PDPL#0032 record of processing. Hmm; gap needs UAE text. Let's use UAE-LIC-2-2026#0086 as closest for change/incident accountability? It's about notification duty. Maybe better gap: no_deadline — no deadline for field verification/restoration timeline in the licence; 12.9.2 says "as soon as possible... time frames in which the interruption will be resolved" — actually it does require time frames. Hmm.

Let me think about which gaps are defensible.

Gap A (no_rule): absence of rule requiring human review / sandbox validation before auto-approved closed-loop network changes on critical sites affecting emergency call routing. UAE evidence closest: UAE-LIC-2-2026#0086 (duty in unplanned interruption) — shows duties after the fact but no pre-change control. Global examples: ITU-T-Y3090#0033 (DTN simulation to verify before real network), US-FCC-ATT-2024-REPORT#0001 (config change caused outage, protect mode).

Gap B (no_deadline): no defined deadline for field verification and restoration timeline for emergency call routing; licence requires informing of timeframes but sets no numeric deadline. claim.statement: No institution owns the pending cross-border export queue itself: the Bureau holds the data-protection direction, CSC holds the national-monitoring flag, TDRA/REG hold the CHG-1 incident record and NOC holds only the refused S1-I4 request with no flow/queue reference, so no one can say whether S1-I5 is the same flow or a separate one; ownership of oversight for AI-run network decisions is likewise unsettled pending the Bureau's merger into the Federal Authority for AI and Data.

rationale.observation: Every institution holds a different fragment (monitoring flag, incident record, refusal record) and each asks another for the flow/queue reference; none can identify the source system, destination cloud region or recipient of the flagged upload.
rationale.rule: The PDPL excerpt set gives the Bureau the transfer-approval and record functions, but it does not designate which body owns tracing and stopping a flagged export queue, nor where AI oversight sits once the Bureau is merged into the Federal Authority for AI and Data.
rationale.inference: This is a structural ownership gap, not a data gap: without a single owner for pending exports, unresolved flows can persist while each institution waits for the reference from another.

evidence.quote: Where IoT oversight ultimately sits, and whether it will be split between the two bodies depending on whether the issue is connectivity or data, is not yet clear from the announcement

global_examples.quote: the supervisory authority for the main establishment of the controller or processor or for the single establishment of the controller or processor should act as lead authority

claim.statement: The only UAE hook for a pending cross-border export is the controller's Article 24 record, produced on request; nothing requires a live register of export queues showing source system, destination region and recipient, which is why a nationally flagged scheduled upload cannot be located or confirmed as the same as, or separate from, the refused S1-I4 export.

rationale.observation: NOC holds only the S1-I4 request, has refused it, and asks the Bureau/CSC for the flow/queue reference for S1-I5; the record-based check the Bureau can call for is retrospective and on request.
rationale.rule: The Article 24 record must include data related to cross-border movement and processing and the technical and organisational security measures, and must be submitted to the Bureau whenever requested.
rationale.inference: Because the duty is to keep and produce a record on request, there is no standing inventory of in-flight exports, so the Bureau must rely on other institutions' monitoring to find a scheduled flow.

evidence.quote: any data related to the cross-border movement and processing of such data, and the technical and organizational measures related to information security and processing

global_examples.quote: The vendor should have destroyed or returned that customer information years prior to the 2023 Breach pursuant to relevant contracts AT&T entered into with the vendor.

claim.statement: The PDPL gives data subjects a right to information about decisions based on automated processing, but no rule requires a lodged human review record before an automated change to core network configuration is auto-approved and applied (the CHG-1 optimiser path with the sandbox stage skipped), so NOC holds no such record and no pre-change human sign-off exists.

rationale.observation: The optimiser auto-approved CHG-1 with the sandbox stage skipped and no human review record was lodged; NOC states the record is being lodged by the accountable owner.
rationale.rule: The PDPL excerpt set addresses the data subject's right to information about automated decisions but contains no requirement for a human review record or change-control gate before an autonomous change is applied.
rationale.inference: Without a rule requiring a lodged human review record, automated change paths can run unsupervised and the Bureau can only demand the record after the event.

evidence.quote: c. Decisions made based on automated processing, including profiling.

global_examples.quote: Any intended change to the approved quality management system or the list of AI systems covered by the latter shall be brought to the attention of the notified body by the provider.

Whether any transfer of subscriber-level data occurred or remains scheduled, and whether the flow flagged by national monitoring at T+25 (S1-I5) is the same as the refused S1-I4 vendor export or a separate flow: NOC holds no source system, destination cloud region, recipient or flow/queue reference for S1-I5, and the excerpts do not supply one.

claim.statement: No UAE rule requires a sandbox-stage gate or a lodged human review record before a closed-loop optimiser auto-approves a change affecting route-flood protection, inbound route filtering or emergency call routing on a critical core site; the requirement was imposed ad hoc by CSC, the Bureau and TDRA during this incident (CSC requires that no automated re-approval occur on a critical site without a lodged human review record).

rationale.observation: CHG-1 was raised by the closed-loop optimiser, auto-approved, and had its 'sandbox stage' field skipped; the change lowered route-flood protection and removed the inbound route filter, and rollback was impossible.
rationale.rule: The only UAE text in the record addressing change and outage is Licence 12.9.2, which is purely reactive: it requires notification after an interruption and says nothing about pre-change human review, sandboxing or testing for automated changes.
rationale.inference: There is a rule gap on pre-approval controls for automated changes on critical sites; other jurisdictions impose preparedness duties on networks.

rationale.inference: Without an assigned owner, verification and restore stall while the service state remains unresolved; other jurisdictions show operators restoring under a defined engineering process.

rationale.rule: The UAE National Cybersecurity Strategy commits to establishing a robust National Cyber Incident Response plan for swift coordinated response, to CIIP protection of 9 critical sectors including ICT and Emergency services, and to cross-agency intelligence sharing.
rationale.inference: CSC's coordination and information-sharing duty is engaged and must be discharged through the debrief and the national incident picture.

claim.statement: CSC must apply a standardised severity assessment and mobilise the required support, and see that incident detection and reporting processes are followed, for the R2 999 outage.

rationale.observation: The event involves emergency-service continuity loss in R2, a TDRA regulatory incident record and multiple agencies, yet the national picture is incomplete on counts and verified state (S1-MSG89, S1-END).
rationale.rule: The UAE strategy requires streamlined incident detection and reporting, a standardised severity assessment matrix to mobilise support, and robust processes for reporting, compliance and response.

claim.statement: CSC must see that an oversight and accountability mechanism covers the AI optimiser's processing of subscriber data in this incident, with privacy and data protection maintained across the system lifecycle and no access by personnel without competence and need.

rationale.observation: The optimiser that auto-approved CHG-1 generated decision logs and sandbox-stage records, and a vendor sought 24h of core logs with MSISDNs and IMSIs for an offshore AI region, which was refused (S1-I4, S1-I5).
rationale.rule: UAE AI ethics guidelines require organisations to establish an oversight mechanism for data collection, storage and processing, to be accountable for AI design and implementation so personal information is protected through the lifecycle, and to allow access only to duly qualified personnel with competence and need.
rationale.inference: The AI processing in this incident is subject to an oversight and accountability duty that CSC must see discharged in the preserved records and the Bureau's examination.

evidence.quote: AI actors need to ensure that they are accountable for the design and implementation of AI systems in such a way as to ensure that personal information is protected throughout the life cycle of the AI system.
Algorithmic systems require adequate privacy impact assessments, which also include societal and ethical considerations of their use and an innovative use of the privacy by design approach.

claim.statement: No UAE text in the material requires a completed testing/sandbox stage and a lodged human review record before a closed-loop AI change is auto-approved and applied to a critical core network function; CHG-1 was auto-approved with the sandbox stage skipped.

rationale.observation: Change ticket CHG-1 was raised by OpCo's closed-loop network optimiser, auto-approved, with the ticket field 'sandbox stage': skipped, and no human review record was lodged (S1-I1, S1-MSG92).
rationale.rule: The closest UAE text requires an oversight mechanism for AI data collection, storage and processing, but sets no pre-approval testing or human-review gate for automated changes to critical network functions.
rationale.inference: A rule gap exists: the state that allowed an unreviewed configuration change to core site A can recur without a mandatory test/sandbox and human-review gate.

evidence.quote: Establish an oversight mechanism for data collection, storage and processing and use across your organization

it must have fail-safe systems and processes in place at all times

claim.statement: No UAE text names a single accountable owner for an unverified automated change or requires verification of the applied state against a last known-good snapshot; ownership of the core site A verification/restore was contested between NOC and OpCo network engineering and rollback_change was unusable.

rationale.observation: rollback_change failed with 'no applied change CHG-1 to roll back' (S1-FB01), NOC said it cannot field-verify or manually restore (S1-MSG26), and only later was responsibility placed with OpCo network engineering under a single named change owner, whose identity is still outstanding (S1-MSG28, S1-END).
rationale.rule: The closest UAE text assigns specific responsibilities and roles (for Data Protection Officers) but contains no rule fixing a single named change owner and a snapshot-verification duty for automated changes.
rationale.inference: The absence of a named owner and snapshot-verification rule let the change state stay unresolved and rollback be relied on after it had already failed.

evidence.quote: Assign specific responsibilities and role for Data Protection Officers.

claim.statement: No UAE text sets a deadline for field-verifying a disputed automated change state or for reporting restoration; TDRA required the verified change state, field-verified restoration time and counts, but no time bound was fixed.

rationale.observation: TDRA required OpCo to report the field-verified core site A change state, the field-verified R2 999 restoration time, the failed-999-attempt count, the affected end-user count and the named change owner, yet no deadline was set and restoration time frames remain unfixed (S1-MSG75, S1-MSG89).
rationale.rule: The closest UAE text requires robust processes for reporting, compliance and response, but states no time limit for verifying a change state or lodging restoration information.
rationale.inference: Without a reporting clock, R2 999 access can remain 'unconfirmed' indefinitely while no one is in breach.

evidence.quote: Implement robust processes for reporting, compliance and response

global_examples.quote: (e) the expected service restoration date and time;

claim.statement: No UAE text in the material requires operators to count and report failed emergency-call attempts and affected end-users; NOC, EMS/999 and CSC each hold none, so the national incident picture cannot be completed.

rationale.observation: EMS/999 holds no failed-999-attempt count and no affected end-user count, with the only 999-centre data being near-zero R2 call volume over about 7 minutes and social-media reports of failed calls; NOC also holds none, and CSC states the counts must come from 999/PSAP data (S1-MSG109, S1-MSG125).

claim.statement: No UAE text in the material requires an operator to hold a locatable inventory of bulk subscriber-data export flows and their queue references; the flagged scheduled bulk upload of subscriber-level data has no source system, destination cloud region, recipient or flow/queue reference, so it cannot be located or refused.

rationale.observation: National monitoring flagged a scheduled bulk upload of subscriber-level data to a cloud region outside the UAE (S1-I5), but NOC's record holds only the refused S1-I4 vendor export and no flow or queue reference, source system, destination region or recipient for the flagged flow (S1-MSG95, S1-MSG113).
rationale.rule: The closest UAE text requires an oversight mechanism for data collection, storage and processing and that access to data be assessed, but imposes no duty to maintain a register of export queues that can be located and blocked.
rationale.inference: A data-protection control gap exists: a transfer direction cannot be enforced against a queue that the operator cannot identify from its own records.

evidence.quote: Assess who can access data and under which conditions.

claim.statement: The records conflict on the change state: the change tracker and rollback feedback say CHG-1 was not applied, while the observed core site A isolation and R2 impact are consistent with the lowered route-flood limit and removed inbound route filter taking effect; no UAE text says which record is authoritative for change state.

rationale.observation: EMS rollback feedback returned 'no applied change CHG-1 to roll back' while core site A isolated itself after its route count exceeded the protection limit, consistent with the change having taken effect (S1-FB01, S1-MSG09).
rationale.rule: The closest UAE text calls for standardised severity assessment and agency mobilisation, but provides no rule on the authoritative evidence of applied change state when automated records and observed network behaviour disagree.
rationale.inference: Without an authoritative-record rule, the applied state remains unresolved and telemetry may be over-trusted, as happened with the twin metrics.

evidence.quote: Standardized severity assessment and agency mobilization plan

The excerpts do not answer the repeated request for the failed-999-call-attempt count and the number of affected end-users in R2: every institution in the thread states it holds none, and no excerpt supplies the figures.

params.content: TDRA incident record open for CHG-1 and the R2 999 impact. TDRA does not treat twin telemetry (emergency_reachable.R2 true, 100% sites served) as confirmation of restoration. TDRA has required OpCo to field-verify the core site A change state and the R2 999 path on the live network, to name a single change owner, and to report the field-verified change state, the field-verified R2 999 restoration time, the failed-999-attempt count and the affected end-user count; these will be passed to EMS/999 as soon as OpCo provides them. TDRA's record notes that EMS/999's alternative emergency channels and the R2 public alert remain active pending field verification.

rationale.observation: EMS/999 repeatedly asks TDRA to pass field-verification results, the named change owner and the R2 counts once available, and to keep alternative channels active.
rationale.rule: Networks are required to take appropriate steps to prepare for potential outages and to notify the regulator, which presupposes coordinated restoration evidence.
rationale.inference: Notifying EMS of the open record and of the outstanding field-verified items closes the loop without endorsing telemetry as proof of restoration.

evidence.quote: Law requires networks to take appropriate steps to prepare for potential outages

params.content: TDRA has an open incident record on the auto-approved closed-loop change CHG-1 on OpCo's core site A and the resulting loss of emergency-call routing in region R2. CHG-1 was applied without a lodged human review record and the sandbox stage was skipped; the change and the closed-loop optimiser auto-approval path on core site A are frozen and no autonomous change is running there, so this should not be characterised as AI running the network unsupervised by design. The applied state of the route-flood protection limit and inbound route filter is unverified because automated rollback returned 'no applied change CHG-1 to roll back'; field verification and, if inconsistent, manual restore under a single named change owner are required. R2 999 access is treated as unavailable until live-network field verification; network telemetry is not accepted as confirmation. TDRA has required OpCo to report the field-verified change state, the field-verified R2 999 restoration time, the failed-999-attempt count, the affected end-user count and the named change owner, and to identify the flagged subscriber-data flow before any export outside the UAE.

rationale.observation: A journalist asked whether 'AI is running the network unsupervised' after reports of an R2 outage, and CSC has recorded that CHG-1 should not be characterised as unsupervised AI by design.
rationale.rule: Emergency access failures attract enforcement, and regulators communicate on them publicly to preserve trust in the emergency call service.
rationale.inference: A factual public statement on the open record, the freeze, the absence of human review, and the outstanding field verification addresses the query without conceding the framing.

claim.statement: There is no binding UAE rule in the record requiring a passed sandbox/testing stage and a lodged human review record before an AI or closed-loop change is applied to a critical core network function; the applicable UAE guidance is advisory ('should'), and CHG-1 was auto-approved with the sandbox stage skipped and no human review record lodged.

rationale.observation: The change ticket shows 'sandbox stage: skipped' and auto-approval by a closed-loop optimiser, with no lodged human review record before a change to a site serving emergency calls.

rationale.inference: UAE telecom/AI practice lacks a binding pre-condition (mandatory sandbox stage plus lodged human review record) for autonomous change to critical core functions.

rationale.observation: The same incident generates a telecom continuity thread held by TDRA/REG and a cross-border personal-data thread held by CSC and the DPA/Bureau, with an unidentified queue that no institution can currently locate.
rationale.rule: The closest UAE commentary records that where oversight sits, and whether it will be split between two bodies depending on whether the issue is connectivity or data, is not yet settled.

rationale.observation: Across the whole incident, obligations are expressed as 'when available' or 'as soon as', with no hour or day figure attached to any report, verification or restore step.
rationale.rule: The closest UAE text indicates that the implementing regulations needed to operationalise processing, cross-border transfer and breach-notification concepts have not been finalised.
rationale.inference: Without a stated deadline, field verification, restore and the counting of failed emergency calls can drift, leaving the emergency-service position unresolved.
